- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day horizon; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.
- Overestimates early in the forecast window after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast by 3–8% for the first 3–5 days post-spike.
- Underestimates late in the horizon (last 5–7 days) — increase forecast by 3–7% to align with observed mean reversion toward higher levels.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing upward momentum; add 1–3 days of delayed price increase in forecast if recent history shows accelerating trend.
- Avoid overfitting to recent low prices; if last 5–7 days are below 55, forecast should not drop below 57 unless strong downward signal exists.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 3–5 consecutive days, increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to avoid underestimating momentum.
- If forecast is below 55 for 3+ consecutive days, add 2–4% to forecast to avoid missing upward bias in mid-to-late horizon.
